weeks.prep: Coffee filters, sand, gravel, activated charcoal (aquarium store), cut plastic bottles, muddy water; petroleum jelly, index cards, string. Do NOT drink filtered water.
misconceptions: Thinking clear water is safe. Filters remove particles but not all germs or dissolved chemicals.
Changing many variables at once.

days.guide: Your child chooses an impact and writes criteria and constraints. Check before moving on: ask "Criteria example?" Look for: Water clarity improves; flow at least 50 mL per minute.

questions.a: Water clarity improves; flow at least 50 mL per minute.

days.guide: Build the filter: gravel, sand, charcoal, filter. Your child tests muddy water. Check before moving on: ask "Role of charcoal?" Look for: Adsorbs some dissolved substances and odors.

questions.a: Adsorbs some dissolved substances and odors.

days.guide: Show how petroleum-jelly cards catch airborne particles. Your child designs a monitoring plan: card locations (kitchen, near a door, bedroom, outside), duration and how to count particles. Check before moving on: ask "Why several locations?" Look for: Compare particle levels.

questions.a: Compare particle levels.

days.guide: Collect the cards after 2–3 days and count particles in a marked square under a magnifier. Run more muddy-water filter tests and record clarity and flow in a table. Check before moving on: ask "How to measure clarity?" Look for: Compare to a scale or count visible particles.

questions.a: Compare to a scale or count visible particles.

days.guide: Your child summarizes results in a paragraph with numbers and proposes two improvements with reasons. Check before moving on: ask "Why test improvements?" Look for: To check they work.

questions.a: To check they work.

weeks.assessment_key: Design notebook: problem, criteria/constraints, design sketch, data table, conclusion, improvements.

weeks.prep: Articles on wildlife crossings (e.g., Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing on US-101) and fish ladders; decision matrix template.
misconceptions: Thinking the 'best' solution is the cheapest.
Ignoring stakeholders.

days.guide: Your child researches solutions for a California species. Check before moving on: ask "Why do mountain lions need crossings?" Look for: Freeways isolate populations, causing inbreeding and roadkill.

questions.q: Why do mountain lions need crossings?
questions.a: Freeways isolate populations, causing inbreeding and roadkill.

days.guide: Your child rates three solutions in a decision matrix. Check before moving on: ask "Criteria?" Look for: Cost, effectiveness, community impact, ecosystem services.

questions.a: Cost, effectiveness, community impact, ecosystem services.

days.guide: Your child redesigns the filter based on test data (changing one variable, such as more charcoal) and compares versions using the same muddy-water sample. Check before moving on: ask "What to compare?" Look for: Clarity and flow rate before and after.

questions.a: Clarity and flow rate before and after.

days.guide: Assign roles (farmer, developer, biologist). Each prepares a 1-minute statement; your child plays the biologist and responds to concerns. Check before moving on: ask "Farmer's concern?" Look for: Land use and water access.

questions.a: Land use and water access.

days.guide: Your child writes a recommendation letter. Check before moving on: ask "Letter must include?" Look for: Recommended solution, evidence, response to concerns.

questions.a: Recommended solution, evidence, response to concerns.

weeks.assessment_key: Matrix: three solutions scored with justification. Letter rubric: clear recommendation, evidence from research, addresses trade-offs, formal tone.

weeks.prep: Tri-fold board; cumulative practice set; final exam.
misconceptions: Display boards with too much text.
Cramming instead of reviewing weak units.

days.guide: Your child creates a display board with problem, design, data and conclusion. Check that graphs are labeled and text is brief. Check before moving on: ask "What goes in the center?" Look for: Data and results.

questions.a: Data and results.

days.guide: Your child presents for 5 minutes to family or a homeschool group and answers at least two questions using data. Check before moving on: ask "How to answer questions?" Look for: Refer to data.

questions.a: Refer to data.

days.guide: Your child makes final terrarium observations and writes what the year-long model revealed about matter cycling and energy flow. Check before moving on: ask "What did the terrarium show?" Look for: Matter cycles; energy from light.

questions.a: Matter cycles; energy from light.

days.guide: Your child completes a cumulative practice set covering all seven units. Review missed items and re-teach. Check before moving on: ask "Exothermic?" Look for: Releases energy.

questions.a: Releases energy.

days.guide: Give the year-end science exam independently. Check before moving on: ask "Photosynthesis products?" Look for: Glucose and oxygen.

questions.a: Glucose and oxygen.

weeks.assessment_key: Presentation rubric: clear problem, design, data, conclusion, answers questions. Final exam: all seven units.
